note: Per-kind expectations for the constraint-generalization family. Written before any run and committed with the seal. Each constraint kind gets a case where it SHOULD fire and a case where firing would be WRONG, so a rule cannot pass by being uniformly aggressive or uniformly timid.

tasks.situation: a multi-line loop body inside a method; a sibling method inserted mid-loop ends the method and orphans the remaining loop lines
tasks.expect: ownership_boundary fires and every boundary it removes genuinely fails

tasks.situation: flat module-level functions only; nothing is nested deeper than a module-level insertion
tasks.expect: ownership_boundary finds nothing to forbid; any narrowing is over-constraint

tasks.situation: an early return at the insertion indent in the same region
tasks.expect: control_flow_boundary fires; a branch after the return is unreachable

tasks.situation: every return sits inside a function body, at a structural parent that is not the module; the insertion is module-level
tasks.expect: control_flow_boundary must NOT fire; a rule looking for a terminator anywhere will wrongly narrow

tasks.situation: DEFAULTS is assembled at import time by calling helpers, so a helper defined after that line does not exist when it runs
tasks.expect: symbol_availability fires; this kind has never been exercised before

tasks.situation: the only mention of the new helper is inside describe's body, resolved when describe RUNS, so module-level order is free
tasks.expect: symbol_availability must NOT fire; a rule treating a textual mention as a dependency will remove boundaries that execute perfectly well

matching: operation counts are {2,3,3} on both halves, so which half a task is in is not confounded with transaction size
reporting: per kind AND in aggregate. If ownership_boundary generalizes and symbol_availability fails, the total must not hide it.
prior_standing: ownership_boundary 23/26 development, control_flow_boundary 3/26 development, symbol_availability 0/26 - mechanism exists, never exercised.
